alex wang: Heads-up: saw a 2-3x spike in p95 decode latency on prod after today's runtime push. dashboard: https://dash.redwood/dashboard/queries/8421 :grimacing:
perf-bot: alert: decode_p95 > 500ms for model=redwood-13B-quant region=us-west-2 (auto-detected at 2200456740)
maya r: which path? prefill or decode?
alex wang: decode path. small-batch workloads (bs=1..4) hit the worst. prefill traces look normal.
jess chen: quick grep — last deploy included PR #3421 (paged->fusion switching tweak + new fusion variant).
sultan: can you paste a small profiler snapshot and the kernel names?
alex wang: here's a quick reproduce command i ran on a dev rig:
```bash
PYTHONPATH=. ./tools/bench_decode.py --model redwood-13B-quant --batch-size 1 --seq-length 16 --warmup 20 --iters 200 
```
And an example per-step log (trimmed):
```
[run] step 001: kernel=flash_fused_paged_qk variant=packed_qk time=6.22ms
[run] step 002: kernel=flash_fused_paged_out variant=packed_out time=5.98ms
[run] step 003: kernel=flash_paged_qk variant=baseline time=2.11ms
[run] step 004: kernel=flash_paged_out variant=baseline time=1.95ms
```
alex wang: note: when the runtime chooses the fused_paged variant we see ~3x per-step cost on short sequences. longer seqs still favor fusion.
maya r: nice repro, thanks. can you attach a nvprof timeline or a small nsight capture? even a perf record stack would help.
alex wang: attached short flame (pasted):
```
flame:  ─┬─ flash_fused_paged_qk 40%
       ├─ attention_forward          25%
       └─ kernel_launch_overhead     10%
```
kai: makes sense — the fusion path emits a larger kernel with extra memory copies for small kv pages. heuristics were tuned for seq>=64. PR3421 relaxed the seq threshold.
jess chen: who owns PR3421? it was me + maya. we set threshold to 32 to avoid cold-start regression on long sequences. didn't test bs=1 short-seq microbench. my bad.
sultan: easy quick test: force the runtime to prefer baseline paged kernels for decode-only flows with bs<=4. can we flip a flag?
alex wang: yep config flag exists: KERNEL_PREF_PAGED_OVER_FUSED=1 (default 0 after PR3421). locally flipping it reduces p95 from ~520ms -> ~180ms for the sampled window.
perf-bot: perf-run summary (dev rig): model=redwood-13B-quant bs=1 seq=16 continuous_batching=on
- before toggle: decode_p95=540ms decode_p50=120ms tokens/sec=18
- after toggle: decode_p95=180ms decode_p50=95ms tokens/sec=22
ops-bot: rolling canary plan suggestion: revert flag in pending rollout and monitor 10% traffic for 30m.
maya r: agree. quick rollback flag is safest. i can push a small config patch to runtime config store.
kai: also add a unit microbench that runs bs=1 seq={8,16,32} on PR CI so we catch this next time.
jess chen: created issue #4567 with repro steps + attach flame + link to PR3421. assigning to me+maya to follow up on threshold logic.
alex wang: tl;dr: regression caused by lowering fusion threshold in PR3421 — fusion is worse for short seqs & tiny batches. plan: flip KERNEL_PREF_PAGED_OVER_FUSED=1 in runtime config (canary), add CI microbench, and update heuristics to be batch-aware not just seq-aware.
maya r: i'll push the config toggle now and open PR for the CI microbench. will post rollout id once done. :thumbsup:
kai: once stable, we can consider a smarter cost model: cost(seq, batch, kv_pages) -> kernel choice. probably need a tiny lookup table populated by offline bench.
sultan: add ops runbook step: if decode_p95 regresses after merges, check recent kernel heuristic PRs and look at PR3421-style threshold edits.
alex wang: thanks all. ping me if the canary shows anything odd. i'll keep collecting traces and start a micro-bisect of fusion variants locally.
perf-bot: follow-up alert scheduled in 10m to verify canary metrics.
ops-bot: rollout queued: cfg_toggle/2026-03-18-rollback-3421 (canary 10%)
alex wang: noted.
